exposure: Patient-controlled analgesia and painless childbirth combined vaginal unprotected program
cohort: 100 primiparous women admitted to the hospital were randomly divided into two groups.
finding: The intervention of patient-controlled analgesia and an unprotected perineum during vaginal birth in primiparas resulted in improved pelvic floor function, reduced pain, shorter labor and hospital stay, and less postpartum hemorrhage compared to acupoint electrical stimulation analgesia.
mod_finding: The 'painless childbirth combined vaginal unprotected program' was associated with improved pelvic floor tissue function, reduced pain, and shorter second stage of labor during vaginal birth compared to acupoint electrical stimulation analgesia.
